purpose: Connect trial probability to the full set of count masses and one selected count.
meaning: A binomial distribution counts successes in fixed independent Bernoulli trials with common success probability. Its mass multiplies a binomial coefficient by the probability of one arrangement of successes and failures.

definition.setting: Each of n independent packets contains a sticker with the same probability p. Count K, the number of packets with a sticker, and select a whole-number count k.

signature.p: Common sticker chance on each independent trial.

conditions: Each of n independent packets contains a sticker with the same probability p. Count K, the number of packets with a sticker, and select a whole-number count k.

Independence, fixed n and a common p are model assumptions. Counts beyond n have zero probability. These masses are at integers; the probability parameter may change continuously without creating fractional packet outcomes.

prompts.prompt: At p=1/2, what is the chance of exactly four stickers among eight packets?
prompts.answer: There are C(8,4)=70 arrangements with four stickers, each of probability (1/2)⁸. Their total is 70/256=0.2734375. The expected count is four, which is not guaranteed.
